title: API gateway: add tier-aware rate limiter + standardized 429 payload + route-group config wiring
author: Amara Diallo
description:
Context: As part of Hot-route capacity protection (ENG-4922), we need consistent, tier-aware throttling behavior at the edge so that (a) enterprise traffic is protected by explicit budgets and (b) best-effort/self-serve traffic is throttled earlier and more predictably, with debuggable semantics for Support and customers.

This PR introduces tier-aware rate limiting in the API gateway, standardizes the 429 response schema/headers across endpoints, and wires initial “route groups” config so we can apply policies at the route level without duplicating per-handler logic.

What’s included: 1) Tier-aware rate limiter: new limiter key-space adds `tier` and `route_group` dimensions. This preserves existing per-account isolation while allowing different defaults for enterprise vs best-effort and different limit shapes per route family (chat vs embeddings vs rerank). 2) Standardized 429 response schema: unified JSON payload + headers for quota/rate-limit throttles. Response includes `error.type=rate_limit_exceeded`, `error.code`, `error.message`, `error.retry_after_ms`, and `error.request_id`. Headers include `Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, and `X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reason` (initial reasons: `tier_ratelimit`, `account_ratelimit`; overload-specific reasons are added in follow-up PR). 3) Route groups wiring: introduces a small mapping layer (config-driven) from request path + method to `route_group` (e.g., `chat_completions`, `embeddings`, `rerank`). This is intentionally low-cardinality and kept stable for dashboards/SLOs.

Non-goals (in this PR): Admission control based on fleet capacity signals (routing-side), overload shedding reason codes, and per-customer exception workflows. Those are handled in ENG-4924/ENG-4923/ENG-4930.

Operational notes: Feature-flagged behind `gateway.rate_limits.tier_aware.enabled` (default off). Config supports tier defaults and optional per-route-group overrides; if a route isn’t mapped, it falls back to `route_group=unknown` and uses existing limiter behavior. Metrics: adds counters for 429s segmented by tier + route_group (bounded cardinality), and latency histogram for limiter evaluation. Logging: adds structured log field `ratelimit.decision` (allow/deny), `tier`, `route_group`, and `policy_source` (default vs override).

Rollout plan: Merge behind flag, enable in us-east canary for allowlisted enterprise accounts, monitor 429 rate + gateway p99 + limiter backend load, then expand region-by-region. Rollback: flip flag off (restores legacy limiter) and/or remove route group mapping file (gateway reload safe).

Testing: Unit tests for key construction + header formatting; integration tests covering (1) enterprise tier getting higher sustained QPS than best-effort for same account, (2) per-route-group overrides, (3) consistent 429 body shape across chat/embeddings handlers, (4) Retry-After correctness.

Follow-ups: (a) overload-specific reason codes + consistent semantics for streaming termination, (b) policy-engine-backed evaluation for quotas, (c) docs updates for customer-facing 429 guidance.
commits: gateway/ratelimit: add Tier enum + tier-aware key builder
gateway/ratelimit: implement route_group mapping + config loader
gateway/metrics: add 429 counters (tier, route_group) + eval latency histogram
tests: add integration coverage for tier defaults and per-route-group overrides
chore: wire feature flag + safe fallback to legacy limiter
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we confirm we’re not introducing unbounded cardinality in metrics? Tagging by account_id would be a non-starter.

Amara Diallo (author): Yep — metrics are tier + route_group + outcome only. Account_id is only used in limiter keyspace (Redis), not in metrics/logging. Added a comment + a unit test to prevent accidental tag expansion.
Cole Summers (review): The 429 schema should align with what Support will see later. Can we keep a stable `error.code` even if we add more reasons later?

Amara Diallo (author): Updated to use stable `error.code=RATE_LIMITED` and `X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reason` for the more detailed reason. Follow-up PR will add overload reasons but keep `error.code` stable.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Where does tier come from? Please confirm it’s derived from auth context and not user input headers.
Amara Diallo (author): Tier is derived from the verified API key / account record (authn middleware), not from request headers. Added explicit guard to ignore any user-provided tier header.
Logan Wright (review): Please add a gateway metric for limiter backend latency; we’ve had Redis tail issues show up as gateway p99 spikes.
Amara Diallo (author): Added `gateway_ratelimit_eval_ms` histogram with buckets tuned for sub-ms expected values, plus a `ratelimit_backend_error_total` counter (bounded labels).
Ravi Menon (review): Route group mapping: do we have a fallback plan if a new endpoint is deployed without a mapping update?

Amara Diallo (author): Unmapped routes go to `route_group=unknown` and use legacy limiter defaults. We also log a warning once per minute per process when `unknown` is hit (rate-limited log) to catch drift during deploys.
Ethan Park (review): Flag behavior looks good. Please ensure we can flip it off without restarting gateways.
Amara Diallo (author): Confirmed; flags are polled and config reload is already hot. Added a short note in internal playbook section on rollback.
Ethan Park (approval): LGTM once CI is green.
Buildkite (CI): integration failed on first run due to flaky timing assertion in Retry-After test; rerun passed after adjusting to allow +/- 250ms tolerance.
release_notes: Gateway: Tier-aware rate limiting (feature-flagged) + standardized 429 payload/headers + initial route-group config mapping for protected endpoints.
related_incident_context: Motivated by noisy-neighbor bursts on /v1/chat/completions causing fleetwide gateway 429 inconsistency and elevated tail latency; this PR unifies throttling semantics and sets the foundation for protected route budgets.
